instruction: Turn off all notifications from the Files application in Ubuntu notification settings.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully enabled Do Not Disturb mode by navigating system tray → Settings → Notifications → toggling the Do Not Disturb switch on. Completed in 5 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system tray, navigate to Settings app, find Notifications section, toggle switches in GNOME Settings
metadata.task_rationale: Harder variation requiring the agent to scroll down in the Notifications panel to find the Files app and toggle its notification off. Tests deeper navigation within the same settings panel.
metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling notifications for the Files (Nautilus) app via Settings > Notifications > Applications list. Evaluator checks the per-app gsettings notification enable flag is false.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses gsettings to read the per-app notification enable flag for Nautilus (Files app) at the correct GNOME dconf path
The 'enable' key is the master per-app notification toggle in GNOME — setting it to false disables all notifications from that app, fully covering the instruction requirement
Metric exact_match correctly compares the gsettings output against expected value 'false\n' (gsettings outputs values with trailing newline)
Expected value 'false\n' is semantically correct for disabled notifications
Single-requirement instruction is fully covered by a single evaluator check
